summary.headline: SPML Infra H1 FY27: operating cash flow of Rs 82.4 crore vs outflow of Rs 44.1 crore a year ago; FY27 guidance of at least 25% growth kept unchanged.
summary.overview: Management reported H1 FY27 operating cash flow of Rs 82.4 crore against an outflow of Rs 44.1 crore in H1 FY26, and cash and equivalents rose 88% to Rs 119 crore from Rs 63 crore at March 2026. Revenue and profit figures were garbled in the transcript and could not be reliably extracted, though management said H1 revenue grew about 45% YoY. Management kept its at-least-25% growth guidance unchanged and said H2 would outperform H1 on revenue and profitability, with monsoon-hit site activity in H1. Order inflow was described as light in Q2; the current order book was cited at about Rs 5,000 crore, with a Rs 186 crore Power Grid 765 kV substation award as the main new win. Management said it is bidding on more than Rs 8,000 crore of BESS and power tenders.

segments.name: Water
segments.commentary: Management said water tenders were limited over the past year but are now picking up, citing Parvati-Kalisindh-Chambal (PKC) linking, Ken-Betwa (Rs 44,605 crore) and Namami Ganga as pipeline drivers. Management also cited expedited JJM funding in states such as Maharashtra and UP.

segments.name: Power transmission and substations
segments.commentary: Rs 186 crore Power Grid award for extension of Harsh 3 and Ramgarh substations in Rajasthan marks entry into 765 kV EHV transmission. Management is also targeting service-station upgrade work in PSU and non-PSU sectors.

segments.name: BESS (battery energy storage)
segments.commentary: Pune facility phase 1 is operational; target is 5 GWh capacity by FY28. Entity C order revenue is expected to start from H2 FY27, with about Rs 300 crore of revenue expected in FY27. A 600-container manufacturing facility is due to be completed by H1 FY28.

guidance_outlook: Growth guidance of at least 25% on both revenue and profit is unchanged; management will update in quarterly calls.
Management expects H2 FY27 revenue and profitability to exceed H1 because monsoon limited H1 site activity.
Management said it expects to cross its guidance this year, but did not raise the number.
Order book target of about Rs 5,000 crore for FY27 is said to be on track; management expects to win one more BESS EPC order this year.
Management expects the next 3-4 years of growth to be around 25% on top line and bottom line, to be updated annually.
Pune BESS expansion: 5 GWh planned, with possible expansion to 5-10 GWh later on order book and market conditions; 25 acres of land acquired with potential of 10-20 GWh.
capex_capacity: BESS battery pack manufacturing in Pune: phase 1 operational; target 5 GWh by FY28.
600-container manufacturing facility: started, completion expected by H1 FY28.
Land of about 25 acres acquired at Pune, with potential to scale to 10-15 GWh or 15-20 GWh per management.
Management said it is not yet pursuing industrial/commercial BESS segment, citing small size of those projects.
demand_pricing: Management said it bids only on contracts with price variation clauses and avoids fixed-price risk on commodity costs.
Management said it avoids projects where margin is below 10%, cash-flow visibility is lacking, or funding is unclear.
Legacy order book of about Rs 1,161 crore is largely subcontracted, with low margins and no working capital exposure; management expects it to complete in FY27-FY28.
New orders with margins above 10% are increasing, per management, and margin trend has improved over the last three quarters.
Management said Rs 8,000 crore-plus of BESS and power tenders are under bid.
Design and drawing approval takes 6-9 months before execution starts, so FY27 order wins will mainly generate revenue in FY28.
Management said O&M margins are higher than EPC margins; EPC/O&M mix in order book is about 95:5 per management.

qa_highlights.question: Why no new orders in the recent BESS tender, and when will commercial production start?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it expects one more BESS order conversion this year, with bids active. Pune phase 1 is operational and revenue from the Entity C order is expected from H2 FY27 at about Rs 300 crore in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company revise its guidance given strong H1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management kept at-least-25% growth guidance unchanged, citing H2 seasonality, and said it expects to exceed it.

qa_highlights.question: How is commodity price inflation affecting margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it only bids on price-variation contracts, so margins are protected; commodity risk is passed through.

qa_highlights.question: Outlook for power segment orders and guidance beyond FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited the 765 kV Power Grid order as the largest new award; service-station and BESS are the two power growth lines. It expects 25% growth over the next few years.

qa_highlights.question: Any update on arbitration awards?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about Rs 100 crore of arbitration awards are at an advanced stage and expected soon, which should reduce debt and improve liquidity.

qa_highlights.question: Is order inflow slowing given JJM budget and tender flow?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said central budget constraints are not a problem because water and power are strategic priorities; it expects Rs 5,000-6,000 crore of orders annually and sizeable water orders in Q3 and Q4.

qa_highlights.question: Are there plans to expand BESS beyond 10 GWh or into other markets?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will stay focused on water, power and BESS for the next 5-7 years and will expand Pune only after the order book supports it.

risks_watch: Order inflow in Q2 was light; the FY27 order target of about Rs 5,000 crore depends on Q3-Q4 wins, mainly water and BESS.
Revenue recognition for new orders is delayed by 6-9 months of design and drawing approval, so FY27 revenue depends on FY26 orders.
Entity C BESS revenue of about Rs 300 crore depends on design approvals and start of H2 FY27 execution.
Government liquidity and the JJM budget run-rate may slow water tender flow.
Arbitration awards of about Rs 100 crore are expected but not yet settled.
Rs 1,161 crore legacy order book needs to be closed out as management guided.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the water and power pipeline and on the cash flow turnaround, but cautious on near-term order inflow and deliberately noncommittal on raising guidance. Several answers on BESS timelines and order conversion were vague, and the transcript is garbled in parts, so some figures should be verified against filings.
key_quotes: Our guidance of at least 25% growth remain unchanged for now and we will keep you updated in our quarterly calls.
H2 contribution more than H1 on both revenue and profitability cumulative which will overall improve our guidance on both top line and bottom line.
As we grow we want the growth to show up in our margin and our cash flow not just in our top line.
